newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Yachting - Peter Campbell's Rhumbline Column.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Yachting - Peter Campbell's Rhumbline Column.

text.p: By Peter Campbell*
BT GLOBAL CHALLENGE RE-START SUNDAY

After two weeks enjoying Sydney hospitality, crews in the BT Global Challenge will head to sea again on Sunday, with the Cruising Yacht Club of Australia despatching the 14 one-design steel 60-footers at 1.30pm from a line just east of the Opera House.

Ahead of them is probably the toughest leg of the race, 6,200 nautical miles from Sydney to Cape Town, five and a half weeks of bashing to windward against the Roaring Forties in the iceberg territory of the Southern Ocean.
The 14 professional skippers were briefed at the Australian Maritime Museum this morning following an informal news conference with CHAY BLYTH, founder of the world's toughest race.

They will then brief the 13 amateur sailors who will be their crews on this rugged leg, including one representative of the major sponsor of each yacht and at least one intrepid journalist, Fremantle-based JOHN (ROBBO) ROBERSON.
ROBERSON, a champion dinghy and one-design keelboat sailor, has joined the crew of Courtaulds International for the leg to Cape Town and will celebrate his 50th birthday at sea in the Indian Ocean.
I'm sure someone will have smuggled aboard a couple of magnums of Mumm for that auspicious occasion -- after all, they are a sponsor.

Courtaulds International turned on a great dinner for their paint customers and yachting media at the CYCA this week to extol their virtues of the anti-fouling paint which has proved so effective on yachts in this round-the-world race but also to meet the crew and view the boat.

As spotlights focussed on the yacht in the CYCA basin, and balloons and smoke (environment free) billowed from the hatchways, one lady guest was heard to ask... the sponsor BT, is that British Tobacco?

BT, of course, stands for British Telecom which has done such a great job with media coverage and communications for this Global Challenge. You can follow the fleet's progress to Cape Town on the Internet -- http://www.btchallenge.com.
ADMIRAL'S CUP CREW HEADS FOR AUCKLAND

Crew members of Australia's Admiral's Cup team will be racing in Auckland this month aboard the ILC40, G Net, which has been chartered by a syndicate headed by Melbourne stockbroker JOHN CALVERT-JONES. G Net will be the mid-sized one-design yacht in the three boat team.

They will sail G Net in the Royal New Zealand Yacht Squadron's Air New Zealand IMS Regatta on Hauraki Gulf and offshore from March 14-23 and will then recommend modifications to be made to the BRUCE FARR designed sloop in NZ before it is shipped to England for the Cowes series in July/August.

Helmsman will be Olympic bronze medalist in Stars, COLIN BEASHEL, while other crew will include his younger brother ADAM, a champion Laser sailor, and DAVID GILES, his Olympic and Etchells crewman. North Sails GRANT SIMMER, who is putting the campaign together, will be tactician while also in the crew will be ROBIN CRAWFORD, best known as the owner of the Sydney to Hobart IMS winner Assassin.

Also competing in the IMS Regatta will be Middle Harbour yachtsman and Internet access adviser RICHARD PERINI who will contest the Mumm 30 class in a brand new yacht just launched by McDell Marine. PERINI sails Addiction, a Mumm 30, out of MHYC.
BEASHEL VERSUS CONNER IN NZ

COLIN BEASHEL is heading for Auckland earlier to contest the inaugural New Zealand championship for the Etchells one-design keelboat class organised by the Pine Bay Yacht Club next week. Looking at the entry list, it could be a repeat not only of previous Etchells world championships but America's Cup clashes.

The two-times world champion Elvina Bay shipwright will racing against another Etchells world champion in DENNIS CONNER, who is flying in from America along with PAUL CAYARD -- all three former America's Cup helmsmen.
CONNER'S tactician and sheet hand will be his former America's Cup arch-rival CHRIS DICKSON. Their local competition will include 1995 America's Cup winning Kiwi skipper RUSSELL COUTTS.

Apart from COLIN BEASHEL, the Australian representation will include Tasmanian NICK ROGERS, a recent recruit to the Etchells following his great international success in Dragon keelboats, including winning a World Dragon Championship and the Seawhanaka Cup and Sayonara Cup match race challenges.

ROGERS, a successful motor vehicle retailer in Hobart, sails from The Royal Yacht Club of Tasmania. He has set a demanding international program this year in the Etchells class and later in the Solings, in which he hopes to represent Australia at the Sydney 2000 Olympics.

Following the NZ Etchells championship, he and his crew, Victorians STEVE JACKSON from Royal Geelong Yacht Club and NOEL DRENNAN from Royal Brighton Yacht Club, will contest world championships for the Solings in Denmark, the Magic 25s in Sydney and the Etchells in Hong Kong in November.
SAILING BOOK OF THE WEEK

Boat Books at Crows Nest (and in Melbourne, Brisbane and Perth) have just received copies of the first book written specifically to cover the changes to the yacht racing rules which come into effect on July 1.

The author is BRYAN WILLIS, chairman of the International Sailing Federation (ISAF) Race Management Committee, who played a major role in formulating the new rules, officially now called the Racing Rules of Sailing (1997-2000)

The Rules in Practice - 1997-2000 includes a special analysis of the major rule changes and a key section explaining the new rules. There are some significant changes, particularly for those who team and match racing and take tactical advantage of the rules. This excellent book looks at the key situations that repeatedly occur on championship courses, from the viewpoint of each helmsman involved in turn, and summarises what each may, must or cannot do.

What you need to know out there on the water are your rights and your obligations, what you are allowed to do, and what you must and mustn't do, writes WILLIS in his introduction and then goes on to explain that with great clarity and excellent illustration.
EXILE FOR MOOLOOLABA

Construction is under way at Boatspeed in West Gosford of the new Farr 50 which SYD FISCHER will charter as the big boat in the Admiral's Cup team. In the meantime SYD and his crew will continue to race and train hard aboard the 50-footer Ragamuffin which he campaigned with such success in the 1995 Southern Cross Cup and the 1996 Kenwood Cup.

The Gazebo Hotel owner who will lead the team at Cowes has entered Ragamuffin for Middle Harbour Yacht Club's 34th annual race from Sydney to Mooloolaba on Queensland's Gold Coast and is looking for his second successive IMS victory to celebrate his 70th birthday.

However, competition will be tough this year with entries including RAY ROBERTS Corel 45, BZW Challenge, and EXILE, the Reichel/Pugh 66 dubbed the mean green machine and owned by WARWICK MILLER, the Australian specialist watch-maker with extensive Hong Kong and Californian business interests.

Exile, which finished second across the line to the record-breaking Morning Glory in the Telstra Sydney to Hobart, recently took line honours in record time and first place on IMS in the CYCA s Sydney to Wollongong race.

Other entries for Mooloolaba include Ord Minet CEO CHRIS GORMAN'S J44, Adria, and the rival owners of Mount Gay 30 class yachts, RAY STONE with Razors Edge and NIGEL HOLMAN with a newly launched Team Fujitsu.

Two wellknown chartered accountants heading north will be CYCA Rear Commodore ED PSALTIS with Midnight Rambler and Royal Prince Alfred Yacht Club immediate Past Commodore Richard Hudson with Indian Pacific. Both have outstanding records in races north, but sailing little half tonners, PSALTIS with Hall Chadwick Nuzulu, HUDSON with Beach Inspector and Public Nuisance.
* Peter Campbell is the editor of Offshore Yachting magazine.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800.
